title: Expose repairs and resynchronization instead of silently discarding data

definition.hypothesis: Every skip, repaired field, inferred duration or rejected metadata element has an explicit reason and input/output range. Separate strict-file fidelity, explicit salvage and live concealment policies.
definition.scope_contract: Start with existing AAC timestamp and AVC/HEVC DTS repairs: emit bounded reason/source-epoch/input-output identities with unchanged-media controls. Then inject junk, truncated init and inconsistent metadata; distinguish strict rejection, requested salvage and live concealment before broadening.
definition.baseline: Current maintained owners at the recorded source revision; unchanged VOD and Shaka policies.
definition.success_criteria: No silent data loss classified as preservation; unchanged path remains byte-identical when valid; repair budget bounded; unsupported semantics return an explicit outcome.
definition.stop_criteria: Do not turn a permissive parser into an automatic arbitrary-file fixer. Avoid implementing validation rules that cannot be sourced or independently checked.
definition.primary_metric: Correct admission, trustworthy diagnostics and fewer hidden fidelity failures; validation overhead measured separately.
definition.negative_control: Inject junk between audio frames, malformed EBML sizes, truncated initialization and metadata disagreements. Compare strict, diagnostic and opt-in repair paths.
definition.effort_limit: This run: canonical deduplication, current-source screening and selected contract probes. Media implementation/qualification is a separate run.

record.reason: Remux records errors/gap skips and performs bounded timestamp/configuration repairs, but there is no uniform input/output-range repair ledger in the inspected native/JS interface. Existing typed route errors distinguish interruption from incompatibility; they do not account for every repaired field or skipped byte.
